learning_outcomes.text: Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.
Adequate knowledge of the concept of business, its institutional and legal framework. Business organization and management.
Ability to learn to work autonomously.
Understand the concepts and characteristics of the company and the entrepreneur.
Know the basic characteristics that define the business environment and knowledge of analysis tools for its understanding.
Understand the business decision-making process, distinguishing the different decision environments and the criteria to adopt in each case.
Know the basic concepts and stages of human resource management in business organizations.
Understand the main decisions made in each of the business subsystems of an organization and understand their interrelationship.
Acquire a general overview of the different current aspects that influence the productive processes of companies.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK I. THE COMPANY AND ITS ENVIRONMENT
TOPIC 1. THE COMPANY AND THE ENTREPRENEUR
Company and Entrepreneur: Concept and Typology
The company system: subsystems in the company
TOPIC 2. THE BUSINESS ENVIRONMENT: SOCIOECONOMIC, INSTITUTIONAL AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK
Techniques for evaluating and adapting to the environment: Strategic planning
BLOCK II: COMPANY ORGANIZATION AND MANAGEMENT
TOPIC 3. THE ADMINISTRATIVE FUNCTIONS OF THE COMPANY
Management and direction in the company
Business decisions: types, circumstances, and styles
TOPIC 4. HUMAN RESOURCES IN THE COMPANY
TOPIC 5. DECISION MAKING IN THE COMPANY (I): THE PRODUCTION FUNCTION
TOPIC 6. DECISION MAKING IN THE COMPANY (II): THE FINANCIAL FUNCTION
The financial function of the company
The financial environment of the company
Concept of investment and its magnitudes
TOPIC 7. DECISION MAKING IN THE COMPANY (III): THE COMMERCIAL FUNCTION
The commercial function of the company and marketing
Influencing factors in the Marketing process. The Marketing plan
teaching_methods: Asynchronous and synchronous activities via virtual classroom platform (videoconference or content)
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is composed of an 80% weight from exams (40% theoretical, 40% practical) and 20% from individual and team activities. A minimum of 4 out of 10 is required for each exam part to be considered, and the average of the theoretical and practical exams must be 5 to pass. For the extraordinary call, the 20% from activities can be carried over if explicitly requested in the first month of the following academic year, but both theoretical and practical exam parts must be repeated. If a student has not participated in continuous assessment, a complementary written test (up to 20%) related to group work activities can be taken in addition to the two final exams. Students may also opt for a single final evaluation exam, covering 100% of the grade, if they meet the regulatory requirements.
